thread:
taylor: Thinking out loud — we need a concrete plan for handling backpressure/quota coupling across our internal APIs during the upcoming model rollout. REST endpoints are choking under bursty traffic; gRPC streams feel more natural but break a few gateway assumptions.
mina: +1. Observed multiple 429s today from the inference frontend when batch sizing spiked. link to logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/err/abc123
joel: Is the problem client-side batching or server-side capacity? We should isolate. If it's backpressure, long-lived gRPC streams can give us more headroom (flow control), but they complicate the API gateway and browser clients.
katherine: Also think about deprecation UX — we can't flip to gRPC-only quickly. Many internal services (and platform scripts) rely on our JSON-over-HTTP endpoints.
seb: Propose hybrid: keep REST for browser/short RPCs, add gRPC for high-throughput internal consumers. Gateway does L7 routing by header: `X-Redwood-Transport: grpc|rest` and enforces quotas per-transport-per-tenant.
mina: Header routing seems easy, but how do we enforce backpressure? Gateway returning 429s will break streaming clients. Need a different signal (HTTP/2 RST? gRPC CANCEL?)
taylor: idea: attach a token bucket at the gateway for REST, and for gRPC expose a per-stream credit API. Client requests credits, gateway decrements, server streams until credit exhausted. Keep quotas unified in the control plane.
joel: That token-credit approach sounds heavier. Could we instead have adaptive drop: gateway responds with `Retry-After` and `X-Backpressure-Mode: drain` header so clients can back off smartly.
katherine: For rollout UX, we should support `x-rollout-canary: <id>` header so we can route a small % to new runtime version and measure latency/cost/quality. Console dashboard should have per-canary panels.
seb: On telemetry: add span tags for transport, batch_size, kv_cache_hit. We need per-route QPS, p50/p95 latency, and ratio of 429 vs 503. Also surface per-tenant quota burn rate.
mina: Also tie eval metrics: if rollout causes quality regressions, auto-fallback. Not just latency/cost but eval signal.
joel: Proto evolution is another snag — if we push gRPC, we must commit to stable protos with clear deprecation windows. Suggest `v1beta` + `v1` headers and server-side compatibility checks during deploy.
taylor: Quick config sketch:
```
route:
  match: /v1/infer
  transports: [rest, grpc]
  backpressure:
    rest_token_bucket: 1000/s
    grpc_credit_limit: 500/stream
  rollout:
    canary_header: X-RW-Canary
    canary_pct: 2
```
katherine: Nice. For the console, UX must show which routes are hybrid, active transport mix, and current backpressure mode. Ops want a single toggle to force `rest_only` for emergency.
seb: Infra-bot: pushing a checklist for this plan would be useful — compatibility matrix, migration docs, SDK updates, telemetry changes.
infra-bot: @channel created checklist ticket RW-4267: `internal-api-backpressure-and-rollout-plan` (links: https://jira.redwood.internal/RW-4267)
deploy-bot: FYI rolling canary on infer-runtime v3 to 2% now. watch `canary:2163948123`
mina: I'll add rate-limiter metrics and per-transport dashboards. Can someone own proto deprecation notices?
joel: I'll handle deprecation schedule and SDK shims (node + python). Will add a migration guide for client teams.
taylor: OK — owners: joel (proto/migration), mina (telemetry/dashboards), seb (gateway/backpressure), katherine (rollout UX). We'll sync next Tue. Thanks all :thumbsup:
